name: Ministerial Structure
description: Iran's ministries divide executive administration among policy portfolios, while ministers serve within a cabinet chaired by the president. The structure requires careful distinction between ministries, other executive organizations, and institutions outside presidential administration.

seo.title: Iran's Ministerial Structure | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Understand Iran's ministerial portfolios, cabinet appointments, and the distinction between ministries and other governing institutions.

content.heading: How ministerial offices are constituted
content.content: A ministry is an executive portfolio with a legally defined remit. Under Article 133 of Iran's constitution, the president nominates ministers for parliamentary confidence; legislation determines their number and powers. Article 134 assigns cabinet coordination to the president. These provisions establish formal responsibilities rather than demonstrating how effectively departments cooperate. [s1]

content.heading: Reading the portfolio names
content.content:
Iran's ministerial terminology contains distinctions that can be unfamiliar to international readers. The Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology are separate portfolios. Health is combined with medical education in another ministry. Petroleum and Energy also appear separately, as do Cultural Guidance and Foreign Affairs. The Iran Data Portal's directory illustrates these distinctions, but its undated list should not be treated as a complete contemporary organization chart. [s2]

This matters when choosing a source: a statement from one ministry cannot automatically establish policy across every institution associated with a broad subject such as education or energy. Readers should identify the named portfolio and the document's date before interpreting its institutional scope.

content.heading: A documented appointment round
content.content:
On 21 August 2024, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported parliamentary approval of all 19 ministerial nominees presented by President Masoud Pezeshkian. Its published list included Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts alongside established economic, social, infrastructure, and security portfolios. This is evidence of the appointment round on that date, not proof that every officeholder or administrative arrangement remained unchanged through the research cutoff. [s3]

The archived English report also contains an apparent translation error in one portfolio label. Its wording therefore needs comparison with Persian appointment records before reuse in a definitive ministry directory. A reliable contemporary directory should pair each ministry's statutory remit with a dated appointment record and verified organizational information. [s3]

name: Legislative Institutions
description: Iran's legislative institutions combine parliamentary deliberation with constitutional and religious review. Understanding the system requires separating elected representation, committee work, executive oversight, and the review of legislation.

seo.title: Iran's Legislative Institutions | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Explore the roles of Parliament, legislative committees, constitutional review, and executive oversight in Iran.

content.heading: An elected chamber within a wider system
content.content: The Islamic Consultative Assembly, commonly called the Majles, is Iran's elected legislative chamber. The constitution permits it to legislate within constitutional limits, while assigning review for compatibility with the constitution and Islamic criteria to the Guardian Council. The Expediency Council addresses specified legislative disagreements between these institutions. A parliamentary vote therefore needs to be distinguished from completion of the legislative process. [s1]

content.heading: Where legislative detail is examined
content.content:
The parliamentary rules reproduced by Syracuse University's Iran Data Portal describe specialized committees as working bodies that examine referred government bills and members' proposals. Their remit also includes investigating implementation, considering questions directed to ministers, and preparing reports. Committee activity thus connects legislative drafting with scrutiny of administration. [s2]

This distinction helps readers interpret parliamentary news. Referral to a committee, publication of a committee report, and approval by the full chamber describe different stages. A report may identify implementation problems or recommend an amendment without itself changing the law. The reproduced rules are useful evidence of procedural design, but their amendment history must be checked before presenting individual procedural details as current. [s2]

content.heading: Formal authority and political participation
content.content:
Institutional powers alone do not explain who can exercise them. The House of Commons Library's March 2024 briefing describes candidate vetting by the Guardian Council and the exclusion of many reformist and moderate candidates. It also explains that parliamentary competition operates through factions and groupings rather than cohesive party blocs comparable to those found in some parliamentary democracies. These observations concern the political conditions of the 2024 election, rather than an assessment of every subsequent parliamentary decision. [s3]

The same briefing distinguishes Parliament from the Assembly of Experts, which has a separate leadership-selection function. Similar English translations of institutional names can obscure this difference: the Assembly of Experts is not another chamber through which ordinary parliamentary bills routinely pass. [s3]

content.title: A simplified map of legislative relationships
content.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  G["Council of Ministers"] -->|"Submits approved government bills"| P["Parliament"]
  M["Members of Parliament"] -->|"Introduce qualifying proposals"| P
  C["Parliamentary committees"] -->|"Submit examination reports"| P
  P -->|"Sends legislation for review"| R["Guardian Council"]
  R -->|"Returns objections"| P
  P -->|"Qualifying unresolved disputes"| E["Expediency Council"]
```
content.summary: The arrows distinguish initiation, committee examination, legislative review, and dispute referral. This diagram summarizes the constitutional framework and reproduced procedural rules; it is not a complete account of deadlines, exceptions, or contemporary institutional practice.

name: Iranian Parliament
description: Iran's Islamic Consultative Assembly, or Majles, is a single-chamber parliament with legislative and executive-scrutiny responsibilities. Its elected membership operates within a system that also gives important review and candidate-screening roles to the Guardian Council.

seo.title: Iranian Parliament: Membership and Powers | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: An introduction to Iran's Majles, its representative role, formal powers, and the documented outcome of the 2024 parliamentary election.

content.heading: What the Majles is
content.content:
The Islamic Consultative Assembly is commonly known as the Majles, a Persian term used for an assembly or council. The Inter-Parliamentary Union classifies Iran's parliament as unicameral: it has a single chamber rather than separate lower and upper houses. Its record for the 2024 election identifies 290 seats contested in a full renewal. [s1]

This institutional identity matters when reading references to other Iranian assemblies. Bodies involved in selecting the country's leadership or reviewing legislation have different functions; they should not be assumed to be additional elected parliamentary chambers. [s1][s2]

content.heading: Legislation and executive scrutiny
content.content:
The constitution gives Parliament powers to investigate national affairs and approve international agreements. It also provides for ministerial confidence votes and questioning. These are formal instruments of scrutiny; their existence does not establish how consistently they produce accountability. [s3]

The August 2024 cabinet appointment round offers a concrete example of parliamentary participation in executive formation: IRNA reported confidence votes approving the president's entire ministerial list. That event demonstrates the use of a constitutional procedure, rather than proving either parliamentary independence or executive control in every case. [s4]

content.heading: Reading the 2024 election record
content.content:
The IPU records voting between 1 March and 10 May 2024, encompassing the initial election and runoff. Its completed election record reports 14 women elected and a principlist majority. These are election-result observations, not a verified membership snapshot for October 2026. Vacancies and other later changes would require separate confirmation. [s1]

The March 2024 House of Commons Library briefing describes the restricted candidate field and the role of factions. This context is essential when interpreting an elected chamber: competition among approved candidates and access to candidacy are separate questions. Readers should also distinguish preliminary reporting from completed results, particularly when an election includes a runoff. [s2]
